question: to the Commission Regina Doherty (PPE) Subject:

The revised electronic Identification, Authentication and Trust Services Regulation (eIDAS Regulation)1 establishes the framework for the European Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet. Given that the EUDI Wallet will be used to store and present highly sensitive personal identity credentials, cybersecurity and user protection are of paramount importance. Strong customer authentication, including multi-factor authorisation, is widely recognised as an effective safeguard against unauthorised access, identity theft and fraud. At the same time, the implementation of the regulation is progressing at different speeds across the Member States, raising questions about the timetable for the availability and interoperability of EUDI Wallets throughout the EU. In the light of the above: 1.

Why did the Commission not require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication and hardware-backed security as mandatory minimum security requirements for access to and use of all EUDI Wallets under the revised eIDAS framework and its implementing acts?

Does the Commission consider the current security requirements sufficient to protect users against sophisticated cyber threats and is it considering introducing mandatory multi-factor authentication requirements in future implementing acts or legislative revisions?

Which Member States are on track to meet the applicable deadlines, which have yet to complete the necessary legislative or technical preparations, and how will Commission ensure timely and consistent implementation?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as regards establishing the European Digital Identity Framework (OJ L, 2024/1183, 30.4.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1183/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.9.2026)

The security requirements for European Digital Identity Wallets follow a security-by-design approach and provide a high level of protection against sophisticated cyber threats. Wallets must be certified at the high level of assurance as set in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/15021, which requires multi factor authentication. Wallets also rely on strong cryptographic authentication, robust device-bound protections and state-of-the-art encryption. Article 5f(2) of Regulation (EU) No 910/20142 requires private service providers in various sectors to accept European Digital Identity Wallets where strong online user authentication is required. The Commission considers the existing framework to provide an appropriate level of security and is not considering introducing additional requirements. It will, however, continuously monitor technological developments and the evolving cybersecurity threat landscape. Member States are under a legal obligation to provide at least one certified EU Digital Identity Wallet to its citizens by 24 December 2026. The Commission has called on Member States to prioritise wallet issuance preparations in order to meet the regulatory deadline. To support Member States, the Commission has made available a set of tools, including a complete version of the Architecture and Reference Framework, the wallet template, and upcoming testing specifications3. The Commission will also organise an interoperability testing event in October 2026.
1 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502 of 8 September 2015 on setting out minimum technical

specifications and procedures for assurance levels for electronic identification means pursuant to Article 8(3) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market (Text with EEA relevance), https://eurlex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2015/1502/oj/eng (point 2.2.1 in the Annex). 2 Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/910/oj/eng. 3 European Commission, European Digital Identity Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework and EUDI Wallet Toolbox, https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/eudi-wallet-toolbox.
